subject.title: Add SQLite snapshot artifacts under backup

question: Should OpenClaw core ship the local `backup sqlite snapshot` artifact contract now, or wait for the Scout/Lobster pilot and keep this as host/plugin-owned for the moment?
rationale: The implementation is a new operator-facing backup/state artifact surface that can expose sensitive session/auth/plugin state, and the PR body explicitly frames the Scout pilot as the evidence checkpoint for whether core, plugin, or both should own the long-term surface.

options.title: Clean branch, then decide core contract
options.body: Require the lockfile and stale-policy cleanup first, then have the storage/backup owner decide whether the cleaned core command can land after reviewing pilot/security evidence.

options.title: Land core snapshot after pilot
options.body: Accept the nested core command if pilot evidence shows full SQLite snapshot artifacts are the right Phase 1 contract for hosted sync.

options.title: Keep it host/plugin-owned for now
options.body: Pause or close the core PR and let the Lobster/Scout plugin path collect more operational evidence before adding a core command.

recommendation.title: Clean branch, then decide core contract
recommendation.body: Require the lockfile and stale-policy cleanup first, then have the storage/backup owner decide whether the cleaned core command can land after reviewing pilot/security evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is closest to the database-first/managed-service direction that this PR cites, while backup owners can still review the command mechanics.
